title: Forced Labour Links in Their Regional Operations
what_it_is: Forced Labour Links in Their Regional Operations

sections.label: Forced labour inquiries into companies
sections.summary: Ministry will investigate Singapore-registered or headquartered companies suspected of breaching domestic forced labour laws if specific information is received.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (a) whether the Ministry has conducted formal inquiries with Singapore-registered or headquartered companies that have been specifically named in foreign legislative hearings or international investigative reports for alleged forced labour links in their regional operations; and (b) if not, whether it will consider doing so.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Foo Cexiang) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade))
sentences.text: We criminalise forced labour in Singapore under various laws.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Foo Cexiang) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade))
sentences.text: Should we receive specific information regarding Singapore-registered or headquartered companies having forced labour links in their operations here or overseas, we will investigate companies suspected of breaching our domestic laws relating to such practices and take enforcement actions if warranted.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Foo Cexiang) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade))
sentences.text: Singapore-registered or headquartered companies are also expected to comply with the laws and regulations of the jurisdictions that they operate in.

sections.label: Singapore advancing international labour standards
sections.summary: Singapore works with the international community and the International Labour Organization on forced labour and will review its domestic regulatory approach.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Foo Cexiang) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade))
sentences.text: Singapore has consistently played a constructive role in advancing international labour standards to address the issue of forced labour at source, including working with the international community and through organisations such as the International Labour Organization.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Foo Cexiang) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade))
sentences.text: We will also review our domestic regulatory approach to ensure that it remains relevant in helping to address this issue.

sections.label: No extraterritoriality, engagement with companies
sections.summary: Singapore's forced labour legislation has no extraterritoriality, but companies operating overseas are told to comply with local laws and engaged when information arises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
sentences.text: First, as I mentioned in my main reply, we do not condone the use of forced labour in Singapore, and our legislation prohibit this and these are our national legislation here.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
sentences.text: We do not have extraterritoriality in relation to these regulations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
sentences.text: However, we inform Singapore-based companies that operate overseas that they need to comply with the laws of the jurisdictions that they operate in.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
sentences.text: Second, should we receive information that our companies are involved in such illegal activities overseas, when necessary, we engage them to understand what it is to ensure that firstly it does not take place in Singapore, and secondly, that they are cooperating with the jurisdictions that they are in to support the investigations there.
